propositions: Cloud transport mutations are not enumerated per-member across retry seams and dispatch levels, creating risk of undocumented retry paths that could cause duplicate writes.
Cloud lacks config-validation tier tests for non-HTTPS URL rejection, missing credential behavior, and resolved-status configurability parity with DC.
Cloud's probe.py hardcodes resolved-status names without runtime configuration hook, preventing deployments with non-standard workflow states from probing correctly.
DC's _USER_SEARCH_METHODS degradation path is unasserted, so accidental renames on Cloud would silently match the same behavior without proof.

Every mutating Cloud transport member must be asserted for exactly one attempt on 429 at its own boundary (REST seam / subprocess seam / dispatch wrapper), with per-member duplicate-write-safety assessment recorded as repo artifact.
New tests must be mutation-checked: concrete perturbations applied to production code must cause each test to fail, proving the test observes its intended boundary and is not blind to retry behavior.
